candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care — interdisciplinary referrals, continuity/coordination of care, client-centered goals, and resource utilization
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — early interdisciplinary palliative-care referral concurrent with active oncology treatment
candidate.educational_objective: Explain that palliative care can be integrated early and concurrently with active cancer treatment to address symptom burden, distress, and quality-of-life needs rather than being reserved only for end-of-life care.

options.A: Palliative care can be added now to address symptoms and quality-of-life concerns while your cancer treatment continues.
options.B: Palliative care should begin only after the oncology team determines that no further disease-directed treatment will be given.
options.C: Palliative care is appropriate only during the last days of life, so symptom management should remain entirely within routine oncology visits for now.
options.D: Starting palliative care means the treatment goal automatically changes to hospice care and all antineoplastic therapy must be discontinued.

candidate.rationale: ASCO's 2024 guideline recommends early referral of patients with advanced solid tumors and hematologic malignancies to specialized interdisciplinary palliative care teams alongside active cancer treatment, particularly when physical, psychosocial, or spiritual distress or quality-of-life concerns are not adequately addressed. NCI likewise states that palliative care may be provided at any point during cancer care and can occur while cancer treatment continues. Palliative care is therefore not synonymous with hospice or an automatic decision to stop antineoplastic therapy.
candidate.source_claim_supported: ASCO recommends early specialist palliative care for patients with advanced cancer alongside active treatment, especially when symptom or quality-of-life needs are present. NCI states that palliative care may be provided at any point in cancer care and patients may continue cancer treatment while receiving it.

candidate.stem: A client with advanced cancer receiving active antineoplastic treatment has persistent pain, nausea, and anxiety. The client says, 'I thought palliative care was only for when cancer treatment stops.' Which response by the nurse is most appropriate?
